display.title: The Plot That Boomeranged
display.summary_short: A wicked prime minister plots to poison the king with the Jews' Purim gift and blame the wise Jewish leader, but his scheme turns back on him.
display.summary_long: In a land near Persia, the foolish King Hakim cares only for his horses and his dog, and leaves the country to his cruel prime minister Zureik, who hates the Jews. The Jewish leader, the wise and kind Chacham Bashi Abu Tzaddik, is also a doctor. When Zureik refuses to judge fairly between two men arguing over a camel, Abu Tzaddik tells a fable about a dog who 'divides' cheese for two cats until nothing is left, and people start bringing their cases to him instead. When a plague of locusts threatens the land, Abu Tzaddik prepares a powder that stops it and tells everyone to thank Hashem, and the king makes him his adviser. Jealous, Zureik and his wife plan to poison the hamantash the Jews send the king for Purim and blame Abu Tzaddik. But Zureik feeds a slice to the king's dog, which goes wild and bites him, and in terror he confesses everything. Abu Tzaddik heals the dog, Zureik is punished, and the king makes Abu Tzaddik prime minister, wishing his Jewish people a happy Purim.
display.lesson: Hashem turns the plans of those who plot against the Jews back on their own heads, as in the Purim story; honesty and kindness win respect.

advisories.note: A prime minister threatens to hang the Jewish leader and expel the Jews, and frames him for poisoning the king.
